subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should native Podman remain a core built-in sandbox backend, or should the existing sandbox registry carry it as an owner-managed Podman plugin with only generic container contracts retained in core?
rationale: Repository policy routes optional integrations through plugin seams when they are sufficient, while this PR introduces a security-sensitive engine implementation, policy semantics, and doctor behavior directly in core.

options.title: Use the plugin boundary
options.body: Keep generic sandbox contracts in core and move Podman-specific CLI, connection, doctor, and lifecycle behavior into a Podman plugin; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Approve a built-in backend
options.body: Explicitly approve Podman as a core-supported engine and document the permanent authorization, upgrade, and security ownership contract before merge.

recommendation.title: Use the plugin boundary
recommendation.body: Keep generic sandbox contracts in core and move Podman-specific CLI, connection, doctor, and lifecycle behavior into a Podman plugin; this is the recommended path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-head refactor owns the central container-backend boundary that this product decision changes.
